feature: op6893 DPMAIF: what the modem fault actually depends on, and what the modem says about it

exception_type_decoding.finding: ex_type 49 is 0x31 = SYS_FATALERR_EXT_TASK_EXCEPTION, not a raw CPU exception. The fixed pc therefore names where a modem task raised the fatal error, not necessarily where the bad access happened.

fatal_record_has_no_file_name.meaning: the modem only fills ex_fatal_v5.filename when is_filename_supported is 1; for this fault it is 0, so the source file is not available and the fixed pc cannot be resolved without modem symbols

modem_image_is_readable_but_not_disassem.access: the md1img partition is visible from mainline as /dev/sdc28 (409600 KiB); its first 64 KiB is byte-identical to the archived md1img-head-64k.bin (sha256 99e69ed3a020a70e7ce6362134c906e8d2cb80a1f0555a1ca7dc41d3be3c45e9)
modem_image_is_readable_but_not_disassem.format: MTK mtk_image: magic 0x58881688 with the name md1rom, then an ext header and FILE_INFO carrying k6893v1_64_k419_20615S_MDBIN_PCB01_MT6893_S00.MOLY_NR15_R3_TC16_S_PR2_SP_V2_P88.bin, which matches the SWVersion the modem prints in its own exception dump
modem_image_is_readable_but_not_disassem.body: everything past the header is high entropy (about 7.2 bits/byte across the whole 32 MiB image), so the code cannot be disassembled. Only plaintext string tables survive, for example ccismcore, dpmaif and DPMAIF around offsets 0x18413ef and 0x184456c
modem_image_is_readable_but_not_disassem.consequence: correlating the fixed pc against the image is not possible on this target

corrected_trigger.superseded_by: evidence/modem-dpmaif-dl-notify-fault.json; the fault is the PIT-update notification written during ring startup, not the ring itself
corrected_trigger.previous_belief: the fault needed both rings running; the driver refused to run both as a workaround
corrected_trigger.measurement: with the modem released and a PDP context active, arming only the downlink ring and sending no uplink traffic at all reproduces the same fault within 10 seconds
corrected_trigger.record: ex_type=49 class=fatal pc=0x91831724 lr=0x91831764 cause=0x40800824 status=0x6002 code=0x305,0x88880302,0xcccccccc sp=0x2904ef00
corrected_trigger.consequence: the uplink ring is not part of the trigger. The one-ring-at-a-time gate does not protect against this fault, because the downlink ring alone is enough. That gate has since been removed: arming the ring without the notification is safe.

fault_addresses.note: every one is unaligned and lies in ordinary AP memory, outside both modem reserved banks reported by lk_regions (cached 0x88000000+0x4960000, noncached 0x8e000000+0x1800000)
fault_addresses.cause_decode: 0x40800824 is HFSR FORCED plus MMFSR DACCVIOL and MUNSTKERR, BFSR UNSTKERR and UFSR UNALIGNED: an MPU denial followed by fault escalation, not a plain bad pointer

second_distinct_modem_failure.when: one run where the uplink ring consumed frames while the downlink ring was armed
second_distinct_modem_failure.record: ex_type=80 (0x50 = ASSERT_FAIL_EXCEPTION) offender=MCU line=591 path=mcu/protocol/lte_sec/errc/lcel/protect/errc_lcel_paging_protect.c lr=0x9073f74a para=0x0,0x0,0x0
second_distinct_modem_failure.note: this is a different exception from the fatal one above, and it is the only case where the modem named a source file

missing_vendor_initialisation_found.function: drv_md_hw_bus_remap() in ccci_dpmaif_drv_v2.c (6.6) and drv_dpmaif_md_hw_bus_remap() in dpmaif_drv.c (4.19), identical in both
missing_vendor_initialisation_found.what_it_writes: AO_MD_DL: REMAP_DOMAIN=0x0101, REMAP_CACHE=0x0607, eight 32 MiB windows spaced 64 MiB apart starting at md_base_at_ap, then MISC_AO_CFG1 bit 0 (DPMAIF_MD_AO_REMAP_ENABLE)
missing_vendor_initialisation_found.state_before: CFG1=0x00000002 so the remap was disabled, REMAP_DOMAIN=0x00000707, all eight MAP registers zero
missing_vendor_initialisation_found.experiment: wrote the vendor-shaped set through poke assuming md_base_at_ap=0x40000000 (0x430041, 0x470045, 0x4b0049, 0x4f004d, 0x530051, 0x570055, 0x5b0059, 0x5f005d); all eleven registers read back exactly
missing_vendor_initialisation_found.result: the fault still occurred, at t=60s with addr=0x3296f00f, same pc, lr and cause
missing_vendor_initialisation_found.status: the remap is genuinely missing, but either the base is not 0x40000000 or the remap is not the cause of this fault

other_vendor_differences.mtu: vendor ccci_drv2_dl_set_mtu writes 3080 (3*1024+8) with BAT_BID_MAXCNT 3; the driver writes 1664 with BIDCNT 1 because the fragment ring was removed
other_vendor_differences.bat_geometry: vendor uses 8192 BAT entries; this driver uses 256
other_vendor_differences.note: both are engine parameters, and the observed fault is on the modem CPU, so neither is a sufficient explanation on its own

allocation_limit.finding: dma_alloc_coherent on this device refuses 4096*1664 (6.8 MB) and 8192*1664 (13.6 MB) with -ENOMEM while 256*1664 (426 KB) succeeds, with 10.4 GB free
allocation_limit.consequence: testing the vendor 8192-entry BAT geometry needs page allocation plus dma_map_single, which is what the vendor does with __dev_alloc_skb

flash_path.boot_partition: /dev/sdc48, 65536 KiB; its first 32 MiB hash equals the flashed boot.img sha256 5986d4d0... so the mapping is confirmed
flash_path.read_only: the initramfs load_root() sets every /sys/class/block/sd* read-only with blockdev --setro, so writing flash from Linux is deliberately unavailable and flashing still requires fastboot
flash_path.fastboot: there is no reboot-mode node, so `reboot bootloader` is not understood by LK; the device had to be taken to fastboot by hand

not_proven: why the modem faults: the remap base is unknown and the remap write alone did not change the outcome
whether the modem ever writes a downlink PIT entry: pit_rd stayed at 1024 and no downlink interrupt ever fired in any run
whether the fault is in the modem downlink send path or in unrelated modem software that only runs once a data context exists
any relationship between the fatal exception and the paging-protect assertion
